Hi GGJJ,

It is always hard to find the place where price will bounce once you find the right FO to trade from. Usually, I look for that last FL or decision point before price fakes out....but I also look at that potential entry point in relation to the size of the FO and the FL Boxes around it to see (visually) if my entry is reasonable. I always ask: Is my entry too far below the place where the FO eventually stops? If so, the risk is pretty high and I may adjust my entry.

I wish I had a concrete answer for exactly how to find the perfect entry every time... but the closest I can get to that is:

Use the last FTR/FL that formed before the FO occurs...you want the last place where price hesitated before shooting up (or down) to form the FO You want the place right before the trick happened...where all the traders got stopped and BO traders got in on the wrong side. You want the "calm" before the storm.

Hope this is useful

I am currently setting entry orders for USD-JPY long: charts to follow with analysis.

When the head of a QM forms as the result of HTF scale clean orders, the shoulders are predictably reactive as the last pocket of orders in that direction are taken. Looking for entry long based on the lower TF ignored level (IQM) that forms just below the compression. Compression is engulfed, we have blue sky northbound.

Entry point has major confluence: IQM on LTF + bullish QM bounce
be careful about your stop to be taken
To manage loss, I should buy @ IQM FL and have a tighter SL just below that FL... thanks Sal
Here is what I am seeing on the higher TG... in terms of SR Flips.

Here is a diagram to show how I incorporate trapped/clean orders with the QM setup. The "HH" (or head) of the QM forming should itself be a reaction to clean orders below it. Once this happens, the LQ left behind by the trapped orders is taken, and the shoulder of that QM is the last pocket of orders remaining.

I saw this happen on UJ perfectly.

This is just a way of tracking where the LQ is likely to be existing so you can position yourself to trade the bounce.
